    Creamy Roasted Red Pepper Pasta

    39
    By Alisa Fleming on October 10, 2026 Alisa's Favorite Dairy-Free Recipes, Dairy-Free Recipes, Entrees, Pasta
    Jump to Recipe
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 5:51
    Instaread

    This dish was on my recipe bucket list for years. I initially spotted the concept in a magazine. Those perfectly twirled noodles had a beautiful blushing hue, but the dish was rich with cream and cheese. Fortunately, I’ve discovered that dairy really isn’t needed to enjoy this insanely delicious meal. I think you’ll agree when you try my dairy-free creamy roasted red pepper pasta recipe.

    Why You’ll Love this Dairy-Free Creamy Roasted Red Pepper Pasta

    • Fast & Easy: I love meals that take less than 30 minutes – don’t you?!
    • Flavorful: The ingredients meld deliciously, but allow the red peppers to take center stage.
    • Perfectly Creamy: Despite the modest fat content, this dish is remarkably rich.
    • Simple Ingredients: Everything is readily available at most grocery stores. You might even have it all on hand.
    • No Dairy or Alternatives: This is a naturally dairy-free creamy pasta!

    Add-In Options

    Of course, it’s delicious as is. But I usually can’t resist adding some of the following proteins and vegetables when I make this dairy-free creamy roasted red pepper pasta:

    • Mushrooms, sauteed
    • Baby Spinach
    • Artichoke Hearts
    • Broccoli Florets, steamed
    • Cauliflower Florets, steamed
    • Zucchini, sauteed
    • Asparagus, steamed or roasted
    • Eggplant, roasted
    • Olives, chopped
    • Fresh Basil, chopped for garnish
    • Fresh Oregano, chopped for garnishChickpeas
    • White Beans
    • Chicken, cooked and chopped
    • Italian Sausage, ground and cooked

    Creamy Substitutions (beyond coconut milk!)

    I settle on light canned coconut milk as my go to in this creamy roasted red pepper pasta for a few reasons. It has a richness similar to half and half, but barely influences the flavor. Since it’s lighter than regular coconut milk, the coconut taste is imperceivable and the pasta is much lower in fat. It’s also very easy to find in almost any store! But here are a few more options that you can substitute for the light coconut milk:

    • Dairy-Free Half & Half: I originally created this recipe with Ripple Half & Half. It’s still available in both shelf-stable and refrigerated versions and it works great.
    • Cashew Cream: I use light coconut milk because it balances with the flavor of the cashews, but you can use all cashews. Increase the cashews to a generous 1/3 cup and use 2/3 cup water or your favorite unsweetened milk alternative (for a little creamier) in place of the coconut milk.
    • Unsweetened Plain Dairy-Free Creamer: Some brands of creamer work great in recipes! I’ve had good luck with nutpods Original (they also have a half & half now, too).

    Recipe FAQs

    Can I use regular canned coconut milk?

    You can, but it will be much richer. If you want similar results, use 1/4 cup full-fat coconut milk + 1/2 cup water to mock light canned coconut milk.

    Can I just use milk alternative?

    If you use regular milk alternative, the result will be a bit less creamy. I would increase the cashews to 1/3 cup. Also make sure the milk alternative is unsweetened and unflavored, and choose a creamier type, if possible.

    Will almonds work instead of cashews?

    They should work fine. They aren’t quite as creamy, and have a slightly more pronounced flavor. But they can lend a tasty romesco sauce vibe! Other good substitutions in this are macadamia nuts and pine nuts. These each have a creamy consistency and blend well. If using pine nuts, you don’t need to grind them in advance.

    Is this Creamy Roasted Red Pepper Pasta spicy?

    It’s a little spicy, but not excessively. Some might call it mild, some might call it medium. You can increase, decrease, or even omit the crushed red pepper depending on the spice level you desire.

    Which brand of roasted red peppers do you use?

    I typically use Trader Joe’s roasted red bell peppers, but I have used other brands. Since brands can vary quite a bit in flavor, taste the red pepper sauce when done and add more salt if it’s lacking depth or lemon juice / balsamic vinegar if it needs a little more zing.

    Can I roast my own bell peppers?

    I use jarred roasted red bell peppers in this recipe for two reasons. One is obviously ease. The second is for seamless depth of flavor. They are typically marinating in oil, vinegar, and / or seasonings, which does influence the taste. If you opt to roast your own bell peppers, you will want to season the dish more.

    Special Diet Notes: Creamy Roasted Red Pepper Pasta

    By ingredients, this recipe is dairy-free / non-dairy, egg-free, optionally gluten-free, optionally nut-free, peanut-free, soy-free, vegan, plant-based, and vegetarian. Just be sure to choose the pasta and creamy ingredients that suit your dietary needs.

    Alisa Fleming

    Dairy-Free Creamy Roasted Red Pepper Pasta

    5 from 7 votes
    This rich and flavorful recipe is a fast, easy, and versatile dinner. Keep in mind that the brand of red peppers you use can affect the flavor. Also, feel free to halve or omit the crushed red pepper if serving timid taste buds.
    Print Recipe Pin Recipe
    Prep Time 5 minutes mins
    Cook Time 15 minutes mins
    Total Time 20 minutes mins
    Servings: 6 servings
    Course: Entree
    Cuisine: American, Italian
    Calories: 327
    Ingredients Method Nutrition Notes

    Ingredients
      

    • 12 to 16 ounces dry pasta (use gluten free, if needed; see Pasta Note below)
    • 2 tablespoons olive oil
    • 1 medium yellow onion chopped
    • 2 garlic cloves chopped
    • ½ teaspoon crushed red pepper
    • ¼ cup raw cashews (see Nut-free Option below)
    • 2 12-ounce jars roasted red bell peppers drained very well
    • ¾ cup lite canned coconut milk (see post above for more options)
    • 1 teaspoon lemon juice or balsamic vinegar
    • 1 teaspoon salt or to taste
    • ⅛ teaspoon black pepper (optional)

    Method
     

    1. Cook the pasta according to the package directions.
    2. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and saute for 4 minutes.
    3. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the garlic and crushed red pepper and saute for 1 minute. Remove the skillet from the heat.
    4. Grind the cashews in a spice grinder until powdered.
    5. Place the ground cashews, drained roasted peppers, coconut milk, lemon juice, and salt in your blender. Puree until very smooth, about 1 minute.
    6. Pour the sauce back into your skillet and cook over medium-low heat, whisking often, for about 5 to 10 minutes, or until lightly thickened. If desired, stir in the black pepper.
    7. Toss the sauce with your cooked pasta to serve.
    8. Store leftover sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. It will thicken more in the refrigerator. You can thin it with water or unsweetened milk alternative, as needed.

    Nutrition

    Serving: 1 servingCalories: 327kcalCarbohydrates: 50gProtein: 9.4gFat: 10.2gSaturated Fat: 3gSodium: 396mgPotassium: 343mgFiber: 3.6gSugar: 5.4gVitamin A: 291IUVitamin C: 81mgCalcium: 24mgIron: 1.6mg

    Notes

    Pasta Note: I use 12 ounces of pasta if I plan on adding in quite a few vegetables and a protein. I use 16 ounces if I'm keeping it simple and just tossing in a modest amount of add ins.
    Nut-free Options: Substitute 2 tablespoons of non-GMO cornstarch for the cashews. Do not overcook the sauce if using starch, as the starch will break down if cooked too long. If you prefer a roux, add 2 tablespoons of flour with the garlic and crushed red pepper. Sauté everything for a minute or two before adding to the blender to smooth out. Let the sauce bubble as needed to reduce to your desired consistency (usually 5 to 10 minutes).
    Cheesy/Depth Flavor Variation: Taste test the sauce, and if more depth of flavor is desired, blend in 1 to 2 tablespoons of nutritional yeast, to taste. I often omit it, but sometimes it works nicely to round things out.
